blocks.why: Normal night at home, 23:30-07:30 local — nothing to work around yet.
Same again; keep the body clock parked on Madrid time before the JFK trip.
Day off, hold the routine so the pre-trip night isn't the first good one.
Full night before the JFK sector; report isn't until 11:25 local so there's no reason to cut this short.
Down at the hotel by 16:00 New York after a 9h45 duty — take two hours now so you can hold out to a local-ish bedtime.
22:30-06:00 New York: first proper night westbound, and it starts nudging you toward local time for the daylight flight home.
23:00-07:00 New York, waking 4h25 before report — this is the sleep that has to carry you through a duty landing at 02:40 Madrid.
Home about 04:45 local; go straight down — 23:00 on the New York clock you've been keeping, so it should come easily.
An hour in the afternoon to top the morning up to about 7h30, without killing tonight.
Back onto Madrid nights — this is the re-anchoring night after JFK.
Clean night before the Boston sector; report 11:25 local so no early alarm.
17:30-01:30 Boston looks strange but it's 23:30-07:30 body time — stay on Madrid, the flight home is a red-eye you have to be awake for.
Mid-morning Boston, mid-afternoon body time — two hours here is what keeps the 24-hour total above 7h30 on a red-eye day.
Two hours before the overnight home, finishing nearly two hours before you leave the hotel so you're clear of the fog.
Home mid-afternoon off the red-eye — two hours only, so tonight still works.
Nine hours to clear the Boston debt before the night flight to Dubai.
Bank two hours in the afternoon — you leave home at 19:00 local for a duty that lands at dawn in Dubai. Two clear hours before you drive.
Straight down on arrival, 08:00-15:00 Dubai — it's your body's morning after a night flight and you'll sleep.
02:30-10:00 Dubai, which is midnight to 08:00 at home — the body-clock night, and you wake with plenty of margin on a 14:50 report.
Home by 23:10 local; nine hours to reset before four days off.
Days off — hold the routine rather than drifting late.
Same pattern, keeping the clock steady.
Last unconstrained night before the Chicago trip.
22:30-06:30 local — an hour earlier than usual because you're out the door at 07:25 for the ORD report.
18:00-01:30 Chicago after an 18-hour day; go with the body clock on night one rather than fighting it.
Ninety minutes to bridge a long Chicago day and let you hold out until a later bedtime tonight.
22:00-05:30 Chicago — shifting later on purpose so you're rested for a departure at 21:50 local.
Two hours before the overnight home, done an hour before you leave the hotel — this puts you above 9h sleep in the 24 before report.
Home about 16:00 local off the red-eye; two hours, then get up and eat so tonight holds.
Nine hours to clear Chicago before the short-haul block.
Deliberately seven hours, not nine — you need to be tired enough to fall asleep at 19:00 tomorrow.
19:00-02:45 local for an 04:35 report; a 19:00 bedtime rarely goes to plan, so treat anything over 6h as a win and don't lie there fighting it.
Airport hotel, not home — the rest is only 10h03 and the 95-minute drive each way would leave you 6h53. Staying airside-adjacent buys the full 8h.
Airport hotel again after a 16h29 duty; 10h01 rest means 8h in bed is only possible if you don't commute.
Go home tonight — 18h46 off and a 13:15 report tomorrow, so nine hours in your own bed after three early starts.
Airport hotel one more time; 10h03 rest into an 04:15 report leaves no room for the drive at either end.
Home and done — nine hours to start paying back what the last five days cost.

conflicts.statement: The roster itself prints this duty as 16h29 (report 02:50 local, off duty 19:19 local, four sectors via ARN and FCO). That is 3h29 beyond the operator's own 13-hour planning ceiling, and the whole first sector sits inside the 02:00-06:00 body-time window.
options: Raise it with crewing before the block starts, not on the day — a 16h29 FDP printed on a published roster looks like a build error rather than a disruption extension.
Ask whether KE526/KE490 (the FCO round trip) can be pulled off the end; that alone brings it to roughly 11h.
If it stands as rostered, file fatigue at the point you accept it, and plan the 26th's sleep at an airport hotel so you start this duty with a genuine 8 hours behind you.

conflicts.statement: Printed duty is 13h09 — nine minutes over the 13-hour ceiling, on the third consecutive pre-06:00 report.
options: Nine minutes is a scheduling rounding problem; flag it with the other two so crewing sees the pattern rather than one stray duty.
Ask for a slightly later report or a shorter turnaround at DUB to bring KE605 inside the limit.
Nothing about your sleep plan changes either way — the 19:30Z start that night is already built to recover from it.

conflicts.statement: Printed duty is 14h18, report 04:15 local, four sectors ending at 18:33 local. That is 1h18 over the ceiling on the last day of a five-day short-haul block.
options: Flag it together with the 27th and 28th — three over-limit duties in five days is a build issue, not three separate ones.
Ask for the MAD-DUB-MAD pairing (KE327/KE401) to come off; that leaves an 8h duty.
If it stands, the 29th's rest must be at an airport hotel or you will start this one on under 7 hours.

conflicts.statement: Off duty 16:47 local, report 04:35 local next day: 10h03 of rest. Your MAD commute is 95 minutes each way, so 3h10 comes out of it, leaving 6h53 of sleep opportunity — 1h07 short of eight uninterrupted hours.
options: Take an airport hotel instead of going home — 30 minutes each way leaves 9h03, which clears the eight hours. This is what the plan above assumes.
If you go home, 117.25(f) puts the call on you: you must tell the operator the rest won't give you eight uninterrupted hours, and you cannot report until you have had one.
Ask crewing to move the 26th's report later or the 25th's release earlier so the rest reaches 12h and the commute stops mattering.

conflicts.statement: Off duty 19:19 local after a 16h29 day, report 05:20 local: 10h01 of rest. Minus the 95-minute commute each way that is 6h51 of sleep opportunity, 1h09 short.
options: Airport hotel again — it takes the opportunity to 9h01 and is the only way this rest works on paper.
This is the tightest rest of the month and it follows the longest duty. If you are going to notify under 117.25(f) once this block, this is the night.
Ask for the 28th's report to move back by two hours; that puts the rest over 12h and inside company policy.

conflicts.statement: Off duty 18:12 local, report 04:15 local: 10h03 of rest into a 14h18 duty. With the commute that is 6h53 of sleep opportunity, 1h07 short.
options: Airport hotel — 9h03 available, and the plan puts you down at 19:00 local for a full eight.
Notify under 117.25(f) if you intend to go home; the shortfall is the commute, not the roster's arithmetic.
The 29th is a short 4h57 duty — ask whether it can move earlier in the day to open the rest up.

conflicts.statement: Rest at base is 10h03, against the company's own 12 hours at base.
options: Cite FCM §4.2.1 when you raise the 8-hour shortfall — the two arguments are stronger together.
Accept it with the airport-hotel plan and treat the 28th's long rest as the recovery point.

conflicts.statement: Rest at base is 10h01, nearly two hours under the 12-hour base standard, and it follows the 16h29 duty.
options: Same conversation as the 26th; ask for the whole 26-28 sequence to be rebuilt rather than patched one night at a time.
If it stands, protect the 18:00Z bedtime hard — no admin, no errands after release.

conflicts.statement: Rest at base is 10h03 against the 12-hour base standard, going into the month's second-longest duty.
options: Raise with the 26th and 27th as a single pattern.
Airport hotel keeps the sleep intact even though the rest itself stays short.

conflicts.statement: Your own line is 9 hours between getting home and leaving again. On the nights of 26, 27 and 29 September the home-to-home window is 6h53, 6h51 and 6h53 — every one of them below your threshold, so by your own rule these are not worth going home for.
options: Book the MAD airport hotel for those three nights; that is what the plan assumes and it is the only version where you get 8 hours.
Move your line for this block only and accept roughly 5h30 in your own bed on those nights — but that breaks the 6-hour main sleep floor three times in five days.
Ask crewing for hotel accommodation at base for the 26-30 block on fatigue grounds, given three duties over the 13-hour ceiling.

conflicts.statement: In the 24 hours ending at release on the 27th you can only get about 6h26 of sleep. The duty is 16h29 long and there is no legal place to put a nap inside it, so the shortfall cannot be planned away.
options: Accept the debt and take the deliberate nine hours on the night of the 28th, which the plan already schedules.
If the FCO sectors come off the end of the 27th, this resolves itself.
Treat the afternoon of the 27th as the low point and plan caffeine and a proper meal around the FCO turnaround rather than relying on alertness.

conflicts.statement: Your 7h30 target is missed on the 27th by about an hour, for the same reason — a 16h29 duty leaves no room.
options: This is the only day in the month the target is missed; everywhere else the plan meets or beats it.
The nine-hour blocks on the nights of the 23rd, 28th and 30th are there to pay it back.

conflicts.statement: Not a breach, but worth knowing you are at the limit: 26, 27 and 28 September are three consecutive pre-06:00 reports. The 29th (13:15 report) is the only thing breaking the run before the 04:15 start on the 30th.
options: If crewing offers to move the 29th earlier to help the rest problem, check it does not create a fourth consecutive early — that trade would cost more than it buys.
Guard the 29th as your recovery day: it is the single night in the block where you get home and get nine hours.
